QCS_REGISTRY.description: Optional registry filter — restricts the QCS search to images and containers under a single container registry. Mapped to the Qualys QQL fragment 'registry:<value>' sent on /csapi/v1.3/images and /csapi/v1.3/containers as the 'filter' query param. Leave blank to search across every registry the QCS subscription has access to.

QCS_REPO.description: Optional repository filter — restricts the QCS search to images and containers under a single repository name. Mapped to the Qualys QQL fragment 'repo:<value>'. Combine with QCS_REGISTRY to scope to a single (registry, repo) tuple. Leave blank to search across every repository in the subscription.

QCS_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional minimum severity floor (info | low | medium | high | critical). Enforced client-side after Faraday severity normalisation (handles Qualys's 1-5 numeric scale — 1=Minimal, 2=Medium, 3=Serious, 4=Critical, 5=Urgent — plus the more familiar critical / high / medium / low / info / negligible tokens upstream feeds carry, with CVSS base-score bucketing as a fallback). The QCS /images and /containers endpoints do not accept a server-side severity filter so the floor is applied after the listing fan-out. Defaults to info (no filtering).

name: qualys_container_security
title: Qualys Container Security
description: Qualys Container Security (QCS) container image + running-container vulnerability REST importer. Pulls findings from a Qualys QCS tenant via the canonical GET /csapi/v1.3/images (image inventory with embedded vulnerabilities array, paginated via pageNo + pageSize, Qualys QQL filtered via 'registry:<value> and repo:<value>') + GET /csapi/v1.3/containers (running container inventory with embedded vulnerabilities array, same pagination + QQL filter shape) endpoints and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON to stdout. Each QCS image bucket (imageId / sha) becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because image scans live on container layers, not on IPs) with hostname = {registry}/{repo}:{tag}@{image_id}; each QCS container bucket (containerId / name) becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because the API does not surface a stable container ip and the container id / name carries the pivot) with hostname = {name}@{containerId}. Per-bucket findings are attached as Faraday vulnerabilities — one per QCS finding (qid + cve + parent) — with [CNAPP] engine prefix, '{cve|QID-<n>} in {package}@{version} on {registry}/{repo}:{tag}' (image scope) or '{cve|QID-<n>} in {package}@{version} on {image|name@id}' (container scope) in the title; description carries vuln_id / qid / package / image|container / severity / status / category / first_found / last_found / published / discovered / vendor / patchable / score / vector. Refs include CWE-* (single + list + list-of-dict shapes with the CWE- prefix collapsed, deduped across finding + meta + parent), finding.link / url / advisoryUrl / vendor_url / nvd_url, and references / links / external_references URL shapes. CVE list harvested via a strict CVE-\d{4}-\d+ regex from finding.cve / cveId / CVE + finding.cveids / cveIds / cves / aliases (string + list-of-string + list-of-dict shapes) + finding.title / description / summary / name (token-scan over free-form strings); deduped case-insensitively. Severity normalised from Qualys's 1-5 numeric scale (1=Minimal -> info, 2=Medium -> medium, 3=Serious -> high, 4=Critical -> critical, 5=Urgent -> critical) and the more familiar critical/high/medium/low/info/negligible tokens upstream feeds carry, with CVSS v3 / v2 base-score bucketing as a fallback when only a numeric cvss / score is given (≤0/>10 -> info, <4 low, <7 medium, <9 high, ≥9 critical); QCS_MIN_SEVERITY enforced client-side after normalisation (no server-side floor — /csapi/v1.3/images and /csapi/v1.3/containers do not accept a severity filter). Status mapped from finding.status / state / vulnStatus — 'Active' / 'New' / 'Reopened' / 'Detected' -> open, 'Fixed' / 'Resolved' / 'Patched' / 'Mitigated' -> closed, 'Disabled' / 'Excluded' / 'Suppressed' / 'Ignored' / 'False_Positive' / 'Risk_Accepted' / 'Deferred' -> risk-accepted (fixInfo.status fallback applied when the top-level status is unrecognised). Auth: Qualys Container Security shares the same identity store as the classic Qualys VMDR / PC / WAS subscriptions; the QUALYS_USER / QUALYS_PASSWORD pair is sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded form data to POST /auth (body 'username=<user>&password=<pass>&token=true') and exchanged for a short-lived JWT (~4 h validity, returned as plain text on the standard QCS gateway, JSON-wrapped under data / token / access_token on some federated stacks — extract_token tolerates both shapes). Subsequent calls send Authorization: Bearer <token>. QUALYS_HOST is the QCS gateway URL for the customer's Qualys platform pod (https://gateway.qg2.apps.qualys.com for US2, https://gateway.qg3.apps.qualys.com for US3, https://gateway.qg1.apps.qualys.eu for EU1).
